__comment: Story-generation catalogue of the game's WORLD PLATES — the ten full-bleed backdrops a player actually stands in front of (five combat arenas, five exploration-map backdrops). One object per image. Written 2026-09-19. Every `description` was written from LOOKING at the shipped file, not from its filename or its provenance record; where a plate carries text or an oddity, the entry says so. Provenance facts (artist/work/licence) are copied from the per-directory provenance.json files and are authoritative there, not here. Enemy portraits (77), character portraits (15), card faces (19), treasure (4), UI splatter motifs (4) and app icons (27) are deliberately NOT in this file — see `scope` below.

_meta.purpose: Input for authoring a new story outline. Each entry pairs what is literally depicted with the narrative hooks it offers, so a story pass can be written against the art the game already has rather than against art it would need commissioned.
_meta.scope: The ten world plates only. Excluded: enemy/character portraits (the engine already carries authored `description` and `causeLines` prose per enemy in axiomancer-mechanics/src/Enemy/enemy.library.ts — read that directly rather than duplicating it here), card faces, treasure icons, UI motifs, and app icons.
_meta.house_register: The Woodcut Codex (axiomancer-mobile/docs/VISUAL_LANGUAGE.md): FromSoftware x Inscryption x illuminated manuscript. Nine of the ten plates are 19th-century wood engravings by Gustave Dore, graded toward the void (grayscale, brightness 0.62 / contrast 1.08). The tenth is flagged.
_meta.how_to_use: For a story outline: read `storySeeds` across all ten entries first — they are written to be combinable. `boundTo` says where in the world each plate already renders, so a beat set in that region already has its backdrop. `coherenceFlag` marks the one asset that does not belong to the house register and should not be used to anchor a beat.

plates.description: Fishermen and boys crowd the rigging and stacked cargo of a moored boat. A forest of masts and dark furled sails fills the upper frame; barrels, coiled rope and nets fill the lower. Most of the figures are looking up and out of frame at something the viewer cannot see. The only light is a pale band of sky behind the masts.
plates.composition: Heavy black at both edges (sails, rigging), one lit sky band across the upper middle.
plates.mood: Working poverty at close quarters. Not menacing — watchful, and slightly expectant.
storySeeds: Everyone in the frame is looking at the same off-frame thing. Whatever the parish is watching, it arrives by water.
A congregation that is also a workforce: the people who owe the parish their labour are the same people who fill its services.
The masts read as a drowned forest. A place that thinks of its boats as trees, or its trees as wrecks.

plates.work: London: A Pilgrimage (1872) — "Over London by Rail"
plates.description: Seen through a dark brick arch: rank upon rank of tenement backyards, each walled, each with its own chimney stack and washing line, receding toward a railway viaduct where a train crosses trailing smoke. Tiny figures stand in the yards. Brick fills almost every surface.
plates.composition: The arch puts near-black at both edges and across the top; a lit corridor runs up the centre to the viaduct.
plates.mood: Grim by ordinary congestion rather than by monsters. Nobody is being tortured; everybody is simply penned.
storySeeds: Every yard is identical and every yard is walled. A city that administers its people in units.
The viaduct passes over the tenements without stopping. Something crosses this district daily and has no business in it — a tax cart, a procession, an inspection.
You are looking through an arch. Somebody built the vantage point you are standing in, which means somebody meant this to be looked at.

plates.work: London: A Pilgrimage (1872) — a dockside night scene
plates.description: Night, or a very low sun. A crowd presses at the lit doorway of a low dockside shed, arms raised. A forest of ships' masts stands behind, black against a grey sky with a single pale sun or moon. A man strides across the open cobbles with a dog at his heel. A body lies face-down in the roadway, unattended. At right, a figure is slumped in a handcart while others stand by.
plates.composition: Dark mass at both lower corners; the lit doorway sits left-of-centre and the pale sky band runs behind the masts.
plates.mood: A queue that has turned into a scrum. Something is being handed out, or handed over, and there is not enough of it.
storySeeds: A body lies in the open and the crowd at the door has not turned around. Whatever is being given out at that doorway is worth more than a death.
This is a crossing you ARRIVE at, not one you watch. The ferry, the queue and the toll are all in the same frame.
The man with the dog is the only figure moving with purpose. He is leaving while everyone else is pressing in.

plates.work: London: A Pilgrimage (1872) — "Dudley Street, Seven Dials"
plates.description: A slum lane crowded almost entirely with children — toddlers held by older children, a girl dragging a toy on a string, infants sitting on the kerb. A goat stands at the left among a knot of women. Rows and rows of second-hand boots are laid out on the pavement and in the gutter, tended by seated dealers. Women lean from upper windows. A cart and a lamppost stand further up the street; chimney stacks recede into haze.
plates.composition: Terraces close the frame at both sides; the roadway opens a lit channel up the middle.
plates.mood: Domestic and dense. Poor, but alive and entirely unbothered by being looked at.
storySeeds: The village's whole visible economy is SECOND-HAND BOOTS. Everything here belonged to somebody else first — including, perhaps, the debts.
This is the only plate in the set where children outnumber adults. A settlement raising the next generation of somebody's obligation.
Someone is watching from an upper window in almost every frame of this street. Being seen is the village's default state.

boundTo: FALLBACK — every region with no rule of its own (currently The Caverns, The Capital, Northern Forest)
plates.description: PIXEL ART, not an engraving. A storm-lit skyline of ruined modern high-rise buildings with lit orange windows, under a saturated violet sky forked with white lightning, behind a foreground of cracked tan stone floor tiles.
plates.composition: Broken walls at both edges; the skyline and lightning occupy the centre; a wide empty tiled floor across the bottom third.
plates.mood: Video-game apocalypse. Reads as a different product from every other plate here.
plates.coherenceFlag: DOES NOT MATCH THE HOUSE REGISTER. It is saturated colour pixel art among nine grayscale wood engravings, and it depicts MODERN high-rise architecture, which no other asset in the game does. It also carries licence UNRESOLVED (owner-supplied, source never traced; tracked in plan/AUDIT.md and covered by THE OPEN GATE 6, which makes replacing it a loop call). Because it is the fallback it is currently the most-seen arena in the game. Do NOT anchor a story beat on it.
storySeeds: Only usable seed: it implies a modern, vertical, electrified civilisation that fell — which contradicts the rest of the world's pre-industrial-to-Victorian register. If the story wants that contradiction it must be deliberate; otherwise this plate should be replaced rather than written around.

plates.description: Colossal chained giants stand and slump around the stone parapet of an enormous well. The nearest rests his head on his folded arm, asleep or exhausted, a heavy manacle and chain at his wrist. Dark water lies at the foot of the wall. At the right, two tiny robed figures stand on a rock slope, included purely for scale.
plates.composition: The giants fill the upper left; the rock slope and the two small figures anchor the lower right.
plates.mood: Vast, restrained, and old. The threat is bound — for now, and by somebody.
storySeeds: The giants are CHAINED, which means someone chained them and someone maintains the chains. The caverns have a warden, or had one.
Two travellers at the size of insects. Whatever the player's business is down here, the place was not built to their scale and does not notice them.
A well implies a bottom. The giants are standing AROUND it, not in it — they are the guards, not the prisoners.

plates.description: A bearded, bare-chested old ferryman braces at the oar of a small boat on rough black water, his cloak slipping from his shoulder. Sheer cliffs rise at the left and the right of frame falls away into pure black. The boat is empty but for him.
plates.composition: Near-total black across the upper right; the lit water and the figure occupy the lower centre.
plates.mood: A working man doing an unpleasant job he has done many times. Not theatrical — practised.
storySeeds: The boat is EMPTY. He is either coming to collect or has just delivered — both are story states.
The ferryman is the game's clearest statement of its own thesis: passage is not free, and the price is set by somebody who will not negotiate.
He is old and still rowing. Nobody has relieved him.

plates.work: Dante's Inferno, Canto I — "I found myself within a forest dark"
plates.description: Enormous tree trunks rise past the top of the frame like columns, their roots knotted over each other. A single robed figure stands small at the base of the largest trunk, turned back to look over one shoulder. Dense undergrowth and briar fill the foreground. A pale shaft of light falls exactly on the figure.
plates.composition: Black trunk mass fills nearly the whole frame; one small lit pocket at centre-bottom where the figure stands.
plates.mood: Lost. The most explicitly subjective plate in the set — it is about a person's situation, not a place.
storySeeds: The figure is looking BACK. The forest is the point at which the road behind stops being an option.
The trees are drawn as architecture — trunks as columns, canopy as vault. A wood that was a building, or a building the wood took.
The light finds the figure rather than the path. Being illuminated here is being exposed, not guided.

plates.description: A street choked to a standstill: omnibuses, drays, barrels, carts and a dense crowd jammed beneath a railway bridge, with a train crossing overhead. A great cathedral dome and spires rise behind through the smoke. Hoardings on the bridge carry large legible advertising.
plates.composition: Dark buildings at both edges; the bridge crosses the upper third; the traffic jam fills the lower half.
plates.mood: Total congestion. Power (the dome) is visible and unreachable behind the crush.
plates.coherenceFlag: Carries LEGIBLE PERIOD ADVERTISING on the bridge hoardings (newspaper mastheads and a company name). It is small in frame and reads as texture at backdrop scale, but it is real English text from 1872 and a close reader will see it. Worth knowing before using this plate in a close-up or a promotional shot.
plates.tags_note: Bound to the generic city|citadel|capital family, so it currently serves BOTH the northern city and the capital on the map screen.
storySeeds: The cathedral is visible from the jam and cannot be reached through it. Proximity to power without access to it.
Everything in the frame is trying to move and nothing is moving. A capital whose actual condition is deadlock.
The train crosses above the jam, unaffected. Two classes of traffic, one of which is never stuck.

plates.description: A narrow slum street packed wall to wall with people. Market stalls and hanging goods line the right; a seated dealer works at a table. A cluster of small children and a dog occupy the foreground, several of the children staring directly out at the viewer. A woman leans from an upper window. The street recedes into haze and chimney stacks.
plates.composition: Tall dark tenements close both sides; the crowd fills the centre; the foreground children are the lightest mass.
plates.mood: Crowded, transactional, and openly observed. The children's direct stare is the plate's strongest feature.
storySeeds: The children look straight out of the frame at the player. The only plate in the set where the world looks back.
A market that is also a home — people are selling in the room they live in. No separation between what you owe and where you sleep.
This is the same street family as the Sweetheart's Village arena. The map and the fight are the same place seen twice, which can be used deliberately: arrive here, then fight here.

recurringMotifs: MASTS AND TRUNKS: the coastal arena's forest of masts, the forest map's columnar trees, and the river arena's massed masts are the same compositional idea three times — vertical dark bars against a pale band. A story can treat the parish's boats and the northern wood as versions of one another.
THE ARCH AND THE BRIDGE: the northern-city arena's brick arch and Ludgate Hill's railway bridge both frame the viewer beneath something crossing overhead. Both cities are places you are UNDER.

THE UNREGARDED BODY: a corpse lies unattended in the river arena and nobody in the crowd turns. Pair with the giants' chains and the ferryman's toll — three images of a system that has already priced a death.
CHILDREN: two plates are dominated by children (Sweetheart's Village, Wentworth Street) and both are the poorest places depicted. The game's inheritance-of-debt theme has its art already.
gaps: NO INTERIOR. Every one of the ten is exterior or subterranean. There is no hall, chamber, church interior or throne room in the world-plate set — so any scene written indoors currently has no backdrop.
NO CAPITAL ARENA. The Capital falls back to the incoherent pixel plate, so the seat of power has no arena of its own. It is the single most story-important region without art.
NO CAVERN ARENA. Same — The Caverns falls back. The map screen has the Titans plate but the fight does not.
NO DAYLIGHT. Every plate is night, dusk, overcast or underground. That is coherent and probably correct for the register, but it means 'the one bright scene' is currently impossible to stage.
